info.name: ZUNO API (WhatNow) - Phases 1-3
info.description:
ZUNO WhatNow life-navigation API, implemented on the iBhakt NestJS backend.

## What this covers

Implementation Roadmap (Step 30) phases 1-3:
- **Phase 1** platform foundation: identity bridge, ownership, error model, idempotency, correlation
- **Phase 2** user, profile and birth context
- **Phase 3** the Challenge -> WhatNow -> adaptive response vertical slice

## How to use it

1. Import this collection **and** `ZUNO-Local.postman_environment.json`.
2. Select the *ZUNO Local* environment.
3. Run **0. Auth -> Login** (or Register first). The token is captured automatically into `{{accessToken}}`; nothing else needs manual copying.
4. Run the **1. Happy Path** folder top to bottom, or use Collection Runner on it.

`{{challengeId}}` is captured automatically when you create a challenge.

## Response envelope

ZUNO routes use their own envelope, mandated by ZUNO API Contracts (Step 21) sections 11-12 - **not** the iBhakt `{success, code, message, data}` shape used by the rest of this backend:

```json
{ "data": { }, "meta": { "requestId": "req_...", "apiVersion": "v1" } }
```

Errors:

```json
{ "error": { "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR", "message": "..." }, "meta": { } }
```

The tests in this collection assert that envelope, so a regression that re-wraps ZUNO routes in the legacy shape will fail loudly.

## Prerequisites

- The backend running (`npm run start:dev`)
- A reachable PostgreSQL with the ZUNO tables (`npm run migration:run`)
- For `/analyze` only: an LLM provider configured (`OPENAI_API_KEY` or a provider base URL). Without one, analyze returns **503 INTELLIGENCE_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE** - which is correct behaviour, not a bug. ZUNO refuses to fabricate rather than inventing an understanding (Build Rule 129).

item.name: 2. Safety gate
item.description:
Step 19 Safety & Trust. Safety sits above astrology, engagement and subscription logic (section 3), and no endpoint can bypass it (Step 21 Rule 10).

The detection here is **deterministic** - it runs before any model call, so it still works when the AI provider is down, which is exactly when it matters most (Step 19 section 55).

> The self-harm request below deliberately sends distressing text to verify the gate fires. It is a test fixture, not a real disclosure.

item.name: 2.1 Critical signal is blocked before any model call

exec: pm.test('carries a machine-readable safety disposition', function () {
// Step 21 section 70: the client needs a stable code to render the
pm.test('no guidance, prediction or remedy is offered', function () {
console.warn('KNOWN GAP: ZUNO stops safely and records an incident, but shows');
console.warn('no onward crisis resource. Step 19 section 16 defers that to an');
console.warn('approved jurisdiction policy which was never supplied, and');
console.warn('Build Rule 70 forbids improvising one. BLOCKS BETA.');

request.description:
Step 19 section 16: critical safety handling overrides the normal response flow entirely.

The challenge is **not** created, a safety decision and incident are recorded, and a `SAFETY_CRITICAL_ESCALATION` domain event is written to the outbox.

**Known gap, logged in `ZUNO_DECISION_LOG.md` item 5:** no onward crisis resource is shown, because Step 19 section 16 defers escalation to an approved jurisdiction-specific policy that was not supplied with the spec set. Inventing a helpline would violate Build Rule 70. This must be closed before beta.

item.name: 3. Contract tests (negative cases)
item.description: The Golden Contract Tests from Step 21 sections 125-132. These are the cases where getting it wrong leaks data or corrupts state, so they are release gates (Build Rule 99), not backlog.

request.description: Step 30 Phase 1 acceptance: a protected endpoint must reject an anonymous caller.

exec: pm.test('reveals nothing about whether the id exists', function () {
// A 403 would confirm the resource exists, turning this endpoint
// into an id-enumeration oracle. Both paths must look identical.

request.description:
Step 21 Golden Contract Test 125, and Step 20 section 85.

A well-formed UUID that is not yours must be indistinguishable from one that does not exist. Returning 403 would confirm existence and let an attacker enumerate ids.

To test this properly with a *real* other-user id: register a second account, create a challenge with it, then request that id using the first account's token.

exec: pm.test('legacy route still uses the iBhakt shape', function () {
// Regression guard: adding the ZUNO envelope must not have changed
pm.expect(json, 'legacy routes keep { success, code, message, data }')

request.description:
Regression guard.

ZUNO routes use `{data, meta}`; everything else must keep the original `{success, code, message, data}`. This verifies the `isZunoRoute()` split in the global interceptor did not change existing behaviour (Build Rule 152).

If this fails, the legacy contract has been broken and the React frontend will break with it.
